extracted.intended_audience: academic researchers seeking Amazon Research Awards / academic institutions applying for Amazon funding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit evaluation dimensions for proposals to the Amazon Research Awards program, which funds academic research projects that leverage computing/cloud resources and advance innovation in areas such as machine learning, robotics, sustainability, and security. The page highlights eligible audience, topical scope, desired impact, and examples of funded work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: academic institutions worldwide
rubrics_metrics.description: Our program supports groundbreaking research across academic institutions worldwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is aimed at researchers affiliated with academic institutions; the site showcases a diverse community of scientists and researchers who have received funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical scope: machine learning, robotics, sustainability, security, and more
rubrics_metrics.description: We're proud to showcase the diverse community of scientists and researchers who have received funding to advance innovation in areas including machine learning, robotics, sustainability, security, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should address topics within (or closely related to) these areas; the listed areas represent examples of fields Amazon funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for groundbreaking / innovative research
rubrics_metrics.description: Our program supports groundbreaking research across academic institutions worldwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amazon highlights projects that advance innovation (e.g., new formulations/algorithms for fairness, efficiency tradeoffs); proposals should demonstrate novelty and the potential to advance their field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrable societal or healthcare impact
rubrics_metrics.description: This project has a huge impact on the society and healthcare because it allows to provide timely and accurate diagnosis of neurological speech disorders (e.g., dystonia).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that can show clear societal, healthcare, or real-world benefits (such as improved diagnosis or services) are exemplified among recipients and therefore align with program goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AWS/cloud compute resources and scaling
rubrics_metrics.description: The MLRA enabled us to use cutting-edge GPU capabilities to develop, train and validate our deep learning models for diagnosis of neurological speech disorders... The generous award provided by AWS has helped us to pump-prime novel research on the interface of climate science and machine learning. It also allowed us to make significant progress in understanding the benefits of using the cloud for ML focused climate research (on clouds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of funded projects leveraged AWS GPU/ cloud infrastructure to scale experiments and conduct compute-intensive research; proposals that propose or demonstrate effective use of cloud resources may be especially relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalability and potential for real-world deployment / field testing
rubrics_metrics.description: The award allowed us to scale up our experiments to learn traffic smoothing algorithms in high fidelity simulations. The RL policies learned from the work are now in the process of being transferred to actual vehicles for field operational testing on California freeways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amazon highlights projects that not only advance research but also scale experiments and demonstrate pathways to field testing or deployment; proposals that describe translational potential or realistic scaling plans align with these examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary or interface research (e.g., ML + climate science)
rubrics_metrics.description: The generous award provided by AWS has helped us to pump-prime novel research on the interface of climate science and machine learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects at the intersection of disciplines (machine learning applied to domain sciences like climate) are represented among recipients; interdisciplinary proposals that leverage ML methods to address domain challenges are within scope.
